chunks: And in the narration of Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said:

key_terms.أَبِيهِ: his father, referring to the preceding Imam in the sanad
key_terms.اَلشُّفْعَةُ: the right of pre-emption in jointly connected property transactions
key_terms.تُورَثُ: is inherited or passed on through inheritance
key_terms.جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام in the chain
key_terms.طَلْحَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ: the narrator Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd in the sanad
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ: Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, the source of the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is the right of shufʿah inherited in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning shufʿah, the right of pre-emption. It states that this right does not pass to heirs by inheritance, making it relevant to questions of financial law and inherited legal claims.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3373 - In the narration of Talhah ibn Zayd from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
